g.title: ActivitySelection
g.text: 1. Which activity do we do next?
How the capture script chooses from Math Academy's queue

g.title: cluster_choice
g.text: Ask these questions in order. The first Yes decides what to do.

g.title: cluster_none
g.text: B. Nothing new is ready to start

g.title: Begin
g.text: Each account makes its own choice

g.title: Boundary
g.text: If the script is already set to resume saved work,
it continues that activity instead of choosing a new one.

a.xlink:title: Open Math Academy's activity queue\nRead the unlocked activities in the order shown\nOpen their details when needed
a.text: Open Math Academy's activity queue
Read the unlocked activities in the order shown
Open their details when needed

g.title: ForcedResume
g.text: Math Academy sends us straight to an unfinished test
Continue from our saved work, if we have it
Otherwise save the problem for investigation

g.title: Metadata
g.text: Are they required, optional, or retakes?
Read Math Academy's notes, question count, and time limit

a.xlink:title: How do we know an assessment is required?\lMath Academy says it is required, or its optional XP allowance is used up.\lIf it is the only activity, has no Notes, and lists a question count\land time limit, the script also treats it as required.\lOtherwise, the requirement may still be unknown.\l\lRetakes are labeled in the title or Notes. Optional assessments\land retakes that aren't required need a question count and time limit.\l
a.text: How do we know an assessment is required?
Math Academy says it is required, or its optional XP allowance is used up.
If it is the only activity, has no Notes, and lists a question count
and time limit, the script also treats it as required.
Otherwise, the requirement may still be unknown.
Retakes are labeled in the title or Notes. Optional assessments
and retakes that aren't required need a question count and time limit.

g.title: History
g.text: Read saved activities and Math Academy's completed lessons/reviews
Remember any lesson or review that lost XP

g.title: TopicRules
g.text: When can we do a lesson on the same topic again?
Usually, we skip a topic's lesson once we've captured it successfully.
We allow another when a repeat is owed after losing XP,
or Math Academy has assigned a new, unstarted lesson for that topic.
Reviews and multisteps can still cover topics we've already captured.

a.xlink:title: Tests used for the final inspection branch are fresh and uncaptured, but need not be capture_supported.
a.text: Set aside activities we can't start as new work
Skip activities the script can't handle, ones already underway,
and ones already saved or completed
Skip lessons we've already captured, with the exceptions at left

g.title: P2
g.text: Choose the first required assessment we can start

g.title: P3
g.text: Choose the first quiz retake we can start

g.title: D4
g.text: 4. Can we choose a lesson or review

g.title: P4
g.text: Choose the lesson or review with the highest score
If tied: lowest Math Academy topic ID wins
For the same topic, choose a lesson before a review
If still tied, choose the first in the queue

g.title: P5
g.text: This is used when scores didn't give us a choice

g.title: P6
g.text: Choose the first available one in the queue
Multisteps are chosen here; they don't get priority scores

g.title: P7
g.text: Choose the first optional assessment we can start
We've run out of the choices above

g.title: D8
g.text: 8. Is there an unstarted assessment left

g.title: Inspect
g.text: The requirement is unclear, or the script can't handle the test
Save the details so the problem can be investigated

a.xlink:title: What makes a lesson or review a higher priority?\lWith self-directed study turned on, the script uses your study goals\land unfinished assignments saved in the math database.\lA topic gets a higher score when:\l- It helps with more of those goals.\l- Fewer unfinished topics remain for a goal it helps with.\l- It is closer to a goal in the chain of prerequisites.\l- An assignment it helps with is due sooner.\l\lThe account's saved Math Academy progress shows which\lprerequisites still need work for this calculation.\l\lWithout those goals, every lesson/review starts with the same\lscore of 1, so the topic-ID rule at left decides.\lLessons and reviews normally all have scores. The next two\lquestions are backups when scoring doesn't choose anything.\l
a.text: What makes a lesson or review a higher priority?
With self-directed study turned on, the script uses your study goals
and unfinished assignments saved in the math database.
A topic gets a higher score when:
- It helps with more of those goals.
- Fewer unfinished topics remain for a goal it helps with.
- It is closer to a goal in the chain of prerequisites.
- An assignment it helps with is due sooner.
The account's saved Math Academy progress shows which
prerequisites still need work for this calculation.
Without those goals, every lesson/review starts with the same
score of 1, so the topic-ID rule at left decides.
Lessons and reviews normally all have scores. The next two
questions are backups when scoring doesn't choose anything.

g.title: Selected
g.text: Save which activity we chose and why
If this repeats a lesson/review that lost XP, aim to get every answer right
Losing XP changes how we answer the repeat; it doesn't move it up the queue

g.title: Recheck
g.text: Check the assessment one more time before starting
Is it still required, a retake, or our last optional choice?
For an optional assessment, check that no lesson, review, multistep,
or other assessment we can start has appeared

g.title: Defer
g.text: Save what changed so we can investigate

g.title: Handoff
g.text: Begin answering and capturing its content

g.title: Recovery
g.text: Check whether a previous capture problem can be fixed
If so, try one repair and read the queue again
If that gives us an activity, go to A

g.title: Resume
g.text: Continue the first saved activity we can resume
Pick up where we left off
Skip activities finished, replaced, already retried, or still blocked

g.title: Nonempty
g.text: Are there still activities in the queue,
and are we running for real?

g.title: Wait
g.text: Wait, then check the queue again
There is work listed, but we can't start it yet

g.title: Finish
g.text: The queue is empty, or we were only checking our choice

g.title: Legend
g.text: Follow the arrows and answer each question
The blue notes explain the rules
A and B point to the sections at the bottom
First in the queue means first on Math Academy's page
